_doc: Assembly rules: how a query that the client builds at run time becomes one representative text.
placeholders.<client>: expression text inside {…} / ${…} -> the text put there (whole client).
file_placeholders.'<root>:<path>': the same for one file; a key '@<line>:<expr>' applies only to the candidate that starts on that line.
assembled: queries written out by hand because the code glues pieces (lists, +=, str.replace); `covers` lists the extracted pieces they stand for.
skip: extracted texts that are not Cypher sent to the server (log lines, messages).

Representative values follow the fixture (corpus/<client>/fixture): Studio's classes are Customer / PurchaseOrder / Supplier under _Entity, its fabric datasource is erp; Robo's labels are the ones its schema scripts declare.

assembled.rule: label probe: one CREATE of up to 40 `(n<i>:_Entity:`<label>`)` patterns, RETURN elementId(n<i>) AS e<i> (two labels shown)
assembled.query: CREATE (n0:_Entity:`Customer`), (n1:_Entity:`Supplier`) RETURN elementId(n0) AS e0, elementId(n1) AS e1

assembled.rule: label probe cleanup: `MATCH (n<i>:`<label>`) WHERE elementId(n<i>) = $e<i>` per label joined with spaces, then `DELETE n0, n1, …`
assembled.query: MATCH (n0:`Customer`) WHERE elementId(n0) = $e0 MATCH (n1:`Supplier`) WHERE elementId(n1) = $e1 DELETE n0, n1

assembled.rule: write_candidate(entity): `_merge_entity_clause('s','s')` = MERGE (s:_Entity:<label> {_source_id: $s_key}) + _ENTITY_SET (ON CREATE SET … / SET updated_at) + SET name = coalesce(…), then RETURN elementId(s)
assembled.query:
MERGE (s:_Entity:Customer {_source_id: $s_key})
ON CREATE SET s.created_at = datetime(), s._confidence = $s_conf,
              s._run_id = $run_id, s._evidence_ref = $evidence_ref,
              s._source_system = $s_sys, s._source_key = $s_skey
SET s.updated_at = datetime()
SET s.name = coalesce(s.name, $s_name)
RETURN elementId(s) AS sid

assembled.rule: write_candidate(relation): subject clause + WITH s + object clause + WITH s, o + MERGE (s)-[r:<predicate>]->(o) with ON CREATE SET / SET, RETURN the three element ids
assembled.query:
MERGE (s:_Entity:Customer {_source_id: $s_key})
ON CREATE SET s.created_at = datetime(), s._confidence = $s_conf,
              s._run_id = $run_id, s._evidence_ref = $evidence_ref,
              s._source_system = $s_sys, s._source_key = $s_skey
SET s.updated_at = datetime()
SET s.name = coalesce(s.name, $s_name)
WITH s
MERGE (o:_Entity:PurchaseOrder {_source_id: $o_key})
ON CREATE SET o.created_at = datetime(), o._confidence = $o_conf,
              o._run_id = $run_id, o._evidence_ref = $evidence_ref,
              o._source_system = $o_sys, o._source_key = $o_skey
SET o.updated_at = datetime()
SET o.name = coalesce(o.name, $o_name)
WITH s, o
MERGE (s)-[r:PLACED]->(o)
ON CREATE SET r.created_at = datetime(), r._confidence = $confidence, r._run_id = $run_id, r._evidence_ref = $evidence_ref
SET r.updated_at = datetime()
RETURN elementId(s) AS sid, elementId(o) AS oid, elementId(r) AS rid

assembled.rule: write_candidate(property): subject clause + SET s.`<prop>` = $value + RETURN elementId(s)
assembled.query:
MERGE (s:_Entity:Customer {_source_id: $s_key})
ON CREATE SET s.created_at = datetime(), s._confidence = $s_conf,
              s._run_id = $run_id, s._evidence_ref = $evidence_ref,
              s._source_system = $s_sys, s._source_key = $s_skey
SET s.updated_at = datetime()
SET s.name = coalesce(s.name, $s_name)
SET s.`grade` = $value
RETURN elementId(s) AS sid

assembled.rule: nl2cypher is LLM-written; only the examples its prompt records: `(po:PurchaseOrder)-[:ORDERED_FROM]->(s:Supplier)` with every node labelled, `RETURN s.name AS supplier, …` named columns, `LIMIT 100`
assembled.query: MATCH (po:PurchaseOrder)-[:ORDERED_FROM]->(s:Supplier) RETURN s.name AS supplier, count(po) AS orders ORDER BY supplier LIMIT 100

assembled.rule: nl2cypher prompt example: a label predicate in WHERE (`WHERE n:Label`, `NOT n:Label`)
assembled.query: MATCH (n) WHERE n:Supplier AND NOT n:PurchaseOrder RETURN n.name AS name LIMIT 100

assembled.rule: pending-design scoped to a bounded context: `_PENDING_QUERY.replace('OPTIONAL MATCH (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(bc:BoundedContext)', '  AND <_SCOPE_BC>\nOPTIONAL MATCH …', 1)`
assembled.query:
MATCH (us:UserStory)
WHERE NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Aggregate)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Command)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Event)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Policy)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:ReadModel)
  AND (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:BoundedContext {id: $scopeId})
OPTIONAL MATCH (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(bc:BoundedContext)
OPTIONAL MATCH (f:Feature)-[:HAS_USER_STORY]->(us)
RETURN us.id AS id, us.role AS role, us.action AS action, us.benefit AS benefit,
       bc.id AS bcId, f.id AS featureId
ORDER BY us.id

assembled.rule: pending-design scoped to a feature: the same replace with `_SCOPE_FEATURE`
assembled.query:
MATCH (us:UserStory)
WHERE NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Aggregate)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Command)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Event)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:Policy)
  AND NOT (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(:ReadModel)
  AND (:Feature {id: $scopeId})-[:HAS_USER_STORY]->(us)
OPTIONAL MATCH (us)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(bc:BoundedContext)
OPTIONAL MATCH (f:Feature)-[:HAS_USER_STORY]->(us)
RETURN us.id AS id, us.role AS role, us.action AS action, us.benefit AS benefit,
       bc.id AS bcId, f.id AS featureId
ORDER BY us.id

assembled.rule: createDatasource: head `CREATE DATASOURCE <name> WITH ENGINE = '<engine>', PARAMETERS = ` + `{<k>: $<k>, …}` over the keys the form filled (password, or credentials when the keychain holds it)
assembled.query: CREATE DATASOURCE erp_new WITH ENGINE = 'postgres', PARAMETERS = {host: $host, port: $port, database: $database, schema: $schema, user: $user, password: $password}

assembled.rule: alterCredentials without a keychain: head `ALTER DATASOURCE <name> SET CREDENTIALS = ` + '{user: $user, password: $password}'
assembled.query: ALTER DATASOURCE erp SET CREDENTIALS = {user: $user, password: $password}

assembled.rule: alterCredentials with a keychain reference: head + '{user: $user, credentials: $credentials}'
assembled.query: ALTER DATASOURCE erp SET CREDENTIALS = {user: $user, credentials: $credentials}

assembled.rule: createVirtualNode with properties: base statement + ` PROPERTIES (<key>, <col> [AS <prop>], …)` (the key column put first when missing)
assembled.query: CREATE VIRTUAL NODE ErpItem IN ontology FROM erp.item KEY item_id PROPERTIES (item_id, name AS item_name)

assembled.rule: known v1 incompatibility the client's own test guards against (10-31 BC full-tree): ORDER BY on a map projection's alias. The clients no longer send it; kept so the answer is on record for v2
assembled.query:
MATCH (bc:BoundedContext {id: $context_id})-[:HAS_READMODEL]->(rm:ReadModel)
RETURN rm {.id, .name} as readmodel
    ORDER BY readmodel.name

params._doc: Parameter values that the rules in prepare.py cannot guess, by query id or by origin. {"$env": NAME} is filled by the runner (COMPAT_PGHOST, COMPAT_PGPORT, COMPAT_PGDATABASE, COMPAT_PGUSER).

fixture_defaults._doc: Derived fixture settings per client. `always`: property values on every derived node; `when_used`: values for a property where the corpus names it for that label; `supplement`: also give each label of the hand-kept fixture two derived nodes carrying every property the corpus names for it.

param_names._doc: Values for parameters by name, per client, used when the query text does not say what the value is (a list after IN, a label name …).
